sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Functional Python and comprehensions are what separate 'I learned Python last month' from 'I write idiomatic Python'. Every fresher who can replace a three-line for-loop with a comprehension signals they understand the language, not just its syntax.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Argument types in Python functions:**

```
def f(a, b, *args, kw_only, **kwargs):
    #  ^  ^   ^        ^        ^
    # pos pos  extra  kw-only  extra
    #          positional       keyword
```

Comprehension = concise loop + optional filter:
`[expr for item in iterable if condition]`

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Mutable default argument trap** — `def f(lst=[])` shares the same list across all calls. Fix: `def f(lst=None): if lst is None: lst = []`.
- **`*args` vs `**kwargs`** — args captures extra positionals as a tuple; kwargs captures extra keywords as a dict.
- **Lambda** — anonymous function, single expression only. Use for sorting key, map/filter callbacks. Never for complex logic.
- **`map()` and `filter()`** — functional builtins; prefer comprehensions in modern Python (more readable).
- **Generator expressions** — `(x*2 for x in range(10))` — lazy, memory-efficient. Use when you don't need a list.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the mutable default argument problem?'** — the most common Python gotcha question at fresher level.
- **'What is the difference between a list comprehension and a generator expression?'** — list builds all at once; generator is lazy/iterable.
- **'When would you use a lambda over a def?'** — for short, single-use functions passed as arguments (sorted key, map callback).
- **'What does `*args` capture?'** — extra positional arguments as a tuple. `**kwargs` captures extra keyword arguments as a dict.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For simple data transformations I use comprehensions — they're more readable than map/filter and avoid the mutable default trap. For reusable logic I use named functions with def. The one gotcha I always warn about is mutable defaults — I always use None as the default and initialize inside the function body."*
